read-build-and-write-first-words.label: Read, Build, and Write First Words
read-build-and-write-first-words.summary: Turn the first sound-spelling patterns into accurate reading, sentence building, and short written Kreyòl responses.

try_read_build_and_write_first_words_ske.prompt: Right after the sketch "Small spelling details count", practice that exact idea with this task. Type the Kreyòl word for “thank you” from memory. Produce the result for write thank you accurately so it reinforces Read, Build, and Write First Words.

read-choice-en.title: Spot en
read-choice-en.prompt: Which familiar Kreyòl word contains the written pattern en?
read-choice-en.hint: Look for the spelling feature practiced in this lesson.

help.concept: Kreyòl spelling keeps meaningful vowel and sound patterns visible in the written word.
help.hint_1: Focus on the spelling pattern named in the lesson instead of applying English spelling habits.
help.hint_2: Compare the letters and accent marks carefully before choosing your response.

read-fill-pen.title: Complete pen
read-fill-pen.prompt: Choose the pattern that completes the Kreyòl word pen.
read-fill-pen.hint: Use the sound-spelling pattern from the lesson to complete the word.

help.concept: Kreyòl spelling keeps meaningful vowel and sound patterns visible in the written word.
help.hint_1: Focus on the spelling pattern named in the lesson instead of applying English spelling habits.

read-listen-mesi.title: Hear mèsi
read-listen-mesi.prompt: Listen, then build the word you hear.
read-listen-mesi.hint: Replay the audio, then rebuild exactly what you hear.

help.concept: Listening practice connects the complete written Kreyòl phrase with the phrase you hear.
help.hint_1: Replay the phrase and keep the words in the same order.
help.hint_2: Listen for the whole word or phrase rather than trying to translate each sound into English spelling.

read-speak-wi-mesi.title: Say a short phrase
read-speak-wi-mesi.prompt: Say the complete Kreyòl phrase shown: Wi, mèsi.
read-speak-wi-mesi.hint: Read the Kreyòl phrase once, then say the whole phrase.

help.concept: When you speak, focus on saying the complete Kreyòl phrase naturally.
help.hint_1: Say the whole Kreyòl phrase clearly at a comfortable pace.
help.hint_2: Use the written Kreyòl as your guide. Say the whole phrase naturally instead of sounding out each letter.

build-bonjou-manman.title: Build a greeting
build-bonjou-manman.prompt: Arrange the Kreyòl words to make “Hello, Mom.”
build-bonjou-manman.hint: Build the complete Kreyòl phrase in natural order.

help.concept: Sentence building uses the same Kreyòl word order and spelling that appear in the target phrase.
help.hint_1: Start with the phrase you recognize, then place the remaining word or punctuation in its natural position.
help.hint_2: Read the complete result aloud once before checking it.

write-mesi.title: Write mèsi
write-mesi.prompt: Type the Kreyòl word for “thank you” used in this lesson.
write-mesi.hint: Write the Kreyòl form exactly as it appears in the lesson.

help.concept: Accurate Kreyòl writing preserves the spelling patterns and meaningful accent marks used in the target words.
help.hint_1: Write the complete Kreyòl form, including any accent mark that belongs in the word.
help.hint_2: Check the vowel spelling one more time before submitting.

read-before-build.title: Recognize the familiar pieces
read-before-build.bodyMarkdown:
Before arranging words, read each piece once. Look for the spellings you already know: **bonjou**, **mèsi**, **wi**, and the nasal patterns in words such as **manman**.

Read each piece, then put the Kreyòl phrase back together in the same order. Keep the spelling you already learned.

write-accurately.title: Small spelling details count
write-accurately.bodyMarkdown:
Writing is where your new visual habits become active. When you type **flè**, keep **è**. When you type **ou**, keep **ou** together.

Now apply those same spelling habits to familiar words from earlier in the module. Do not add English spelling conventions that are not present in the Kreyòl word. Short, accurate answers are better practice than long guesses.

first-phrase.title: Combine familiar words
first-phrase.bodyMarkdown:
You can already combine a few familiar words into tiny meaningful phrases. **Bonjou, manman.** means “Hello, Mom.” and reuses sound patterns from this module.

Read the phrase, build it from the word bank, then write one of its familiar words from memory. That is the same sequence you will use in later modules with longer sentences.
